chunks: And likewise, Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Washa, and he was one who held the view of Waqif (stopping).

Then he returned (to belief in the Imamate). The cause of his return was that he said: I traveled to Khorasan for my trade. When I arrived, Abul Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) sent to me asking for a striped cloth. It was among my clothes, but its presence had been hidden from me. I said: I do not have any of it with me. The messenger returned and mentioned its sign and that it was in such-and-such bundle. I searched for it and it was as he said, so I sent it to him. Then I wrote some questions that I wanted to ask him. When I reached his door, he came out to me with the answers to those questions which I intended to ask him, without me having revealed them to him. He returned from the statement of Waqf to the certainty of his Imamate.

key_terms.إِمَامَتِهِ: His Imamate: The spiritual and temporal leadership and authority of the Imam.
key_terms.الْقَطْعُ: Al-Qat': Certainty or definitive knowledge, as opposed to doubt or speculation.
key_terms.الْوَقْفُ: Waqf: The doctrine of stopping or halting, specifically referring to those who believed the Imam had died without appointing a successor.
key_terms.حِبْرَةٌ: Hibrah: A type of striped cloth, often from Yemen, used as a valuable commodity in trade.

ai.seo_question: What miracle convinced Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Washa to accept the Imamate of Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: This narrative from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the conversion of Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Washa, a prominent figure among the Waqifiyyah who initially hesitated to accept Imam al-Rida’s continued life. The miracle of the hidden cloth (*kaff*) and the Imam’s knowledge of unspoken questions served as decisive proofs of his divine knowledge (*ilm al-ghayb*), solidifying his Imamate in the eyes of his contemporaries. This event underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Imam’s supernatural awareness as a key criterion for validating his spiritual authority during periods of occultation.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 77 - In the same way, Hasan bin Ali Washa was also a Waqifite of his time;

then he returned to belief in the twelve Imams and repented for his past mistakes; the cause of his repentance, as he himself states, was that: I traveled to Khorasan for business. When I reached there, Abul Hasan Ridha (a.s) sent someone and asked me for the striped cloth from Yemen. It was among the merchandise that I was having, but I had forgotten it, so I said: I don’t have any striped cloth. The Imam’s messenger went away, but returned again to inform me that I was having it in so and so bundle; I found it at the same place and sent it to the Imam. After that I wrote some questions, which I wanted to ask him. Just as I reached his place, the Imam emerged from inside and mentioned to me the replies of the questions, which I wanted to ask him and about which no one knew anything. On witnessing this miracle, Hasan bin Ali Washa gave up his Waqifite beliefs and adopted faith in the Imamate of Imam Ridha (a.s).
